title: A Noetherian local ring of dimension one is regular iff it is a normal domain
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring of Krull dimension $\dim A=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $A$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] (its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by one element) if and only if $A$ is a normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] (an integral domain integrally closed in its field of fractions).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr, line 29104), equivalence of (3) and (5), with its proof

proof.text: Assume A is regular local. The existing instance IsRegularLocalRing.isDomain, recorded at [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], gives the domain property. Apply IsRegularLocalRing.isDiscreteValuationRing A hdim, recorded at [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr], to obtain a discrete valuation ring.

From the domain and DVR instances, Mathlib typeclass inference supplies IsIntegrallyClosed A. This is the standard DVR-to-principal-ideal-domain-to-integrally-closed instance chain (Stacks 00PD, (1) implies (5)); in Lean the whole assembly is exact ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩.

Conversely, install the assumed IsDomain A and IsIntegrallyClosed A instances. Since dim A = 1 implies dim A ≤ 1, apply the already proved IsRegularLocalRing.of_isIntegrallyClosed A, a declaration recorded at [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr]. That declaration directly supplies regularity, so no separate principal-maximal-ideal lemma is needed. Combine the two directions using the constructor of the equivalence.
